'''Tom Boyd''' (April 1903 – 6 December 1991) was a [[shipyard]] worker, [[Patternmaker (engineering)|patternmaker]], [[trade unionist]] and  [[politician]] in [[Northern Ireland]].

After studying at [[Belfast Technical College]] and [[Queen's University, Belfast]], Boyd became prominent in the [[United Patternmakers' Association]]. Joining the [[Northern Ireland Labour Party]] (NILP), he stood for election to the [[Belfast]] [[Board of Guardians]] in 1933.

In the [[1938 Northern Ireland general election|1938 Stormont elections]], Boyd stood unsuccessfully in [[Belfast Victoria (Northern Ireland Parliament constituency)|Belfast Victoria]].  In the [[1945 United Kingdom general election|1945 UK general election]], he stood for the Westminster seat of [[Belfast East (UK Parliament constituency)|Belfast East]], taking 43.6% of the vote.  He stood for the seat again in [[1950 United Kingdom general election|1950]], [[1951 United Kingdom general election|1951]] and [[1955 United Kingdom general election|1955]], but never came so close to election.

In the [[1949 Northern Ireland general election|1949 Stormont election]], Boyd stood in [[Belfast Bloomfield (Northern Ireland Parliament constituency)|Belfast Bloomfield]], and in [[1953 Northern Ireland general election|1953]], he stood in [[Belfast Pottinger (Northern Ireland Parliament constituency)|Belfast Pottinger]].  He finally won this seat in [[1958 Northern Ireland general election|1958]], and on election he became the leader of the NILP, a post he held until finally losing his seat at the [[1969 Northern Ireland general election|1969 election]].

Following his defeat, Boyd led the [[Presbyterian Church of Ireland]] Social Services Committee until 1978.
